rules.title: Repeated connector pin functions differ
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Pins with matching meaningful normalized functions on repeated connector symbols, or within one symbol, use different or missing net assignments. A complete source-matched project interface map can supply a return role when native function text is absent, generic Pin_N, or numeric-only; this can compare returns across different connector symbols. The same map can compare generic or numeric-only supply contacts across symbols only when their exact authored voltage_domain values match. Numeric function text can identify a comparable contact within an exact repeated symbol by itself, but does not establish an electrical role. Generic KiCad Pin_N labels remain unknown unless the source-matched map supplies a supported role. When every participating connector has a current source-matched peer_assignment_group, non-return and non-supply comparisons are partitioned by that group; return and supply role comparisons remain cross-group. Incomplete or stale group coverage retains the unscoped comparison.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Matching functions are only candidate evidence; the rule cannot decide whether nets must be common, bonded, or isolated.

Project-mapped return roles are used only from a complete interface entry whose catalog digest, component pin inventory, native pin functions, and net assignments match the current native netlist; role classification still does not require commonality.

Project-mapped supply roles are compared across symbols only when a complete source-matched interface map supplies the same exact voltage_domain text for both contacts. A matching role and domain prompt review; they do not prove that nets must be common or that independent, switched, ORed, or isolated sources are invalid.
A numeric function such as 7 is compared only as matching native function text within an exact repeated symbol; it does not mean ground, supply, or a required common connection.

A peer_assignment_group scopes which connector instances are compared; group membership does not require their nets to match, and distinct groups do not assert that their nets must remain separate. A review basis is required, and incomplete or stale group evidence does not suppress the broad comparison.
Without a source-matched interface role, absent functions and generic Pin_N placeholders do not establish matching roles; exact-symbol peer assignment rules handle those contacts at lower confidence.

Automatic candidates are numeric J/P/X/CN references and symbols in standard Connector libraries except Connector:TestPoint; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can additionally classify a custom symbol. Other aliases and library families can evade candidate discovery.
References listed as DNP by the native netlist are excluded from population-dependent comparisons.

rules.title: Comparable connector peer pin has an outlier assignment
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: Among fitted connector instances using the exact same library symbol, or distinct symbols sharing one nonempty native PART_ID with matching nonempty value and footprint, complete identical pin inventories, and matching nonempty per-pin native function and electrical-type metadata, the same pin number is unconnected on an outlier peer or differs from a unique most-common schematic net assignment shared by at least two instances; at least one compared function is absent or a generic Pin_N placeholder. When every participating connector has current source-matched peer_assignment_group evidence, comparisons are partitioned within each group; incomplete or stale group coverage retains the unscoped comparison.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Identical symbol and pin number identify comparable contacts but do not establish a required common net; per-port isolation, optional contacts, and unused pins can be intentional.
A tied most-common assignment does not identify an outlier and is delegated to connector.peer_pin_assignment_divergence.

A peer_assignment_group identifies comparison scope only; it does not establish a required common net. Distinct groups are excluded from comparison only while all participating connector group reviews are current and complete.

Cross-symbol comparisons require a shared native PART_ID plus matching nonempty value, footprint, complete pin inventory, and matching nonempty function and electrical-type metadata for every pin. Missing or inconsistent metadata leaves that alias group ineligible; matching identity still does not establish a common-net requirement.

Automatic candidates are numeric J/P/X/CN references and symbols in standard Connector libraries except Connector:TestPoint; an exact project-reviewed interface reference can additionally classify a custom symbol. Other aliases and library families can evade candidate discovery. Missing symbol identity or pin-number inventory can evade comparison.
The check is limited to cases where at least one peer has absent or generic Pin_N function metadata and does not establish PCB copper connectivity or off-board wiring.
DNP connector instances are excluded, and the result remains a review hint subject to project rule overrides or an exact ignore.

A peer_assignment_group identifies comparison scope only; it does not establish a required common net. Distinct groups are excluded from comparison only while all participating connector group reviews are current and complete.

This is a graphical review hint only; it does not infer electrical intent, replace native ERC, or move/edit text. The rule is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions.

rules.title: Electrical wire crosses a free-text envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic geometry with standard-stroke glyph metrics measured from the digest-pinned native SVG exporter

limitations: Only top-level free text using the standard KiCad stroke font, 95 printable ASCII glyphs and measured U+00B0, U+00B1, U+00B5, U+00D7, U+03A9, and U+2014 glyphs, positive explicit font sizes, horizontal text, and centered/left/right justification is measured. Plain KiCad escaped line breaks are supported. Custom faces, bold or italic text, custom thickness, markup, other characters, unsupported justifications, rotations, and other drawing object types produce partial geometry coverage. KiCad serialized \n and \r line-break escapes are detected before metric lookup.

A guarded axis-aligned text envelope can intersect a wire even when individual glyph strokes do not. Native SVG fault/control evidence validates the tested crossing only; intentional annotation-over-wire layouts remain possible.

The rule examines native wire segments only, not buses, labels, symbol fields, pin names or numbers, symbol graphics, or PCB geometry. It is a graphical review hint, not an electrical finding or connectivity change. It is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions.

rules.title: Free text overlaps a symbol-body envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 text glyph metrics and supported embedded symbol graphics
rules.predicate: Report top-level, supported free-text glyph envelopes overlapping a supported symbol-body envelope by at least 0.1 mm2 after a 0.1 mm text-edge guard and 0.15 mm symbol-body guard.
limitations: Only top-level free text using the standard KiCad stroke font, 95 printable ASCII glyphs and measured U+00B0, U+00B1, U+00B5, U+00D7, U+03A9, and U+2014 glyphs, positive explicit font sizes, horizontal text, and centered/left/right justification is measured. Plain KiCad escaped line breaks are supported. Unsupported text styles, other characters, unsupported justifications, or rotations leave geometry coverage partial. KiCad serialized \n and \r line-break escapes are detected before metric lookup.

Symbol-body envelopes support rectangles, polylines, Bezier curves, circles, and non-degenerate three-point arcs. Unsupported or degenerate symbol primitives leave geometry coverage partial. Both text and symbol geometry use axis-aligned envelopes; disjoint or non-rectangular primitives and gaps between glyph strokes can produce candidates, including intentional annotations over symbols.
Labels, symbol fields, pin names, sheet text, and other text objects are outside this rule. It is a graphical review hint, off by default, and does not establish connectivity or design intent.

rules.title: Electrical wire crosses a symbol-body envelope
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound KiCad 10.0.5 or 10.0.6 schematic wire geometry and supported embedded symbol graphics
rules.predicate: For supported single-unit, single-conversion symbols with rectangle, polyline, bezier, circle, or non-degenerate three-point arc graphics, report a native wire centerline that remains at least 0.2 mm inside the axis-aligned body envelope and overlaps it for at least 0.3 mm.
limitations: The envelope bounds supported embedded symbol graphics after orthogonal rotation and x/y mirroring. Bounding several disjoint or non-rectangular primitives can include empty space; valid connector contacts inside a symbol outline and other intentional wire crossings can be review candidates.

Text graphics, collinear or degenerate arcs, multi-unit or multi-conversion symbols, unsupported transforms, or unrecognized body primitives leave geometry coverage partial. The rule does not infer pin connectivity, intended isolation, or schematic electrical meaning.
This is a graphical review hint only. It is off by default and supports project review, block, off, and exact-ignore dispositions; it never edits the schematic or replaces native ERC.

rules.title: Strapped I2C address differs from the project map
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored responder and address-pin map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For a mapped strapped responder with exact symbol, bus-pin, address-pin-function, and low/high-net evidence, the resolved 7-bit address differs from the project-declared address.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule checks only responders and address-pin bits explicitly mapped by the project; it does not infer device addresses from references, values, or part names.
A source-bound netlist cannot establish firmware-selected addresses, off-board devices, boot-time changes, or mux topology absent from the project map.
A mapped symbol function is library metadata; correctness of the part pinout and project-authored address basis still requires review.

rules.title: Mapped I2C responders share a static address on one segment
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored segment and responder map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native netlist evidence
rules.predicate: Two or more fitted, completely mapped responders on the same project-declared SDA/SCL segment resolve to the same 7-bit static address.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Same-address responders on different declared segments are allowed; correctness of mux isolation and completeness of the segment map remain project review responsibilities.
Dynamic, unresolved, DNP, unlisted, off-board, or firmware-addressed devices do not produce collision findings; unresolved and dynamic entries remain coverage gaps.
The rule identifies address conflicts, not bus electrical compatibility or successful communication.

rules.title: Likely I2C responder is missing from the project address map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported symbol pin functions and net assignments
rules.predicate: For a component not marked DNP with a U or IC reference, at least one uniquely assigned SDA function pin and one uniquely assigned SCL function pin on distinct nets, report it when the project address map is absent or does not list that reference.

limitations: The reference-prefix filter is limited to U and IC; other designator conventions are not discovered.
Only exact SDA, I2C_SDA, SCL, and I2C_SCL symbol function spellings are recognized after punctuation normalization; incorrect or missing library metadata can evade the prompt.

A component with SDA and SCL functions may be a bridge, translator, or other part that does not need a static address. This is a review candidate and does not assert that every such device is an addressable responder.
A mapped responder is treated as covered even if its pins or identity mismatch; the project-map comparison reports those separate source mismatches.

rules.title: Likely UART endpoint is missing from the project peer map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported pin functions, exact net assignments and names, fitted state, and the source-hashed project serial-peer contract
rules.predicate: Report an unmapped fitted TX/RX candidate through either bounded path: (1) exact exported TX/TXD and RX/RXD pin-function pairs on distinct uniquely assigned nets within one component; or (2) one fitted U/IC pin on each distinct uniquely assigned UART/USART-labeled TX/RX net, with both nets also assigned to at least one common fitted connector candidate, when the exact pin pair is absent from the project serial_peers map. The label path is skipped when the MCU pin already exports a recognized serial function.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The pin-function path recognizes only bounded TX/TXD and RX/RXD spellings. The net-label path recognizes only exact UART/USART labels with optional channel digits and TX/RX suffixes; bare TX/RX labels, arbitrary aliases, missing net labels, and differently named channels are outside the predicate.

The net-label path requires exactly one fitted U/IC pin per role and a common fitted connector candidate on both nets. Ambiguous assignments, multiple candidate MCU pins, mismatched labels, absent connector candidates, and non-unique assignments are excluded.

Names and exported pin functions are discovery clues, not proof of protocol or endpoint intent. Unused MCU alternate functions, other serial standards, incomplete documentation, or labels that do not reflect the intended circuit can produce or suppress prompts.

A serial-map endpoint suppresses only its exact TX/RX pin pair; the separate source-bound serial contract reports wrong identity, pin, or net mappings. A map does not prove board copper continuity or external wiring.

This heuristic does not establish that a peer, connection, shared ground, voltage domain, or UART requirement is intended. It does not discover missing power or reference pins; those require connector inventory and authored pinout coverage.

rules.title: Likely SPI participant is missing from the project device map
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including exported symbol pin functions, net assignments, and the source-hashed project electrical contract
rules.predicate: For a non-DNP U- or IC-prefixed component, report a likely SPI participant when at least one uniquely assigned clock function (SCK/SCLK), one uniquely assigned data function (MOSI/SDI/COPI or MISO/SDO/CIPO), and one recognized chip-select function (CS/CSN/NCS/NSS/SS/SSEL/CE0/CE1) are present, and the reference is absent from the project-authored SPI controller/device/bridge roster or no required roster is configured.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The reference-prefix filter is limited to U and IC; other designator conventions are not discovered.
Only the listed exact pin-function aliases are recognized after punctuation normalization and an optional SPI prefix; missing or different library metadata can evade the prompt.
A controller, translator, multi-protocol device, or intentionally unused SPI-capable IC can match. The result is a coverage prompt and never asserts that the component must join an SPI bus.
A reference in the authored roster is considered covered even if its signal pins are wrong; the SPI contract comparison reports those separate mismatches.
This schematic-netlist check does not prove PCB copper continuity, internal transfer behavior, signal timing, or firmware configuration.

rules.title: SPI peers use different voltage-named supply rails
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including complete native pin-type inventories, exact SPI pin functions, pin/net assignments, and an optional source-hashed digital-peer voltage contract
rules.predicate: For fitted U- or IC-prefixed parts with complete native pin-type inventories and exactly one assigned positive power_in rail per part, report a REVIEW prompt when an exact recognized SPI signal function joins an output-capable pin to an input-capable pin and the two rail labels each contain exactly one explicit positive voltage token with different parsed nominal values. Suppress only exact endpoint/net/symbol/footprint matches with complete authored LINT-061 output and input limits.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Voltage values are parsed from exactly one token in each native net name and are review clues only; they do not establish actual rail voltage, source validity, tolerance, logic thresholds, output guarantees, or incompatibility.

Only U/IC references, exact normalized SPI clock/data/select aliases, known native input/output/bidirectional/tri-state signal types, complete pin-type inventories, and one assigned power_in supply net are supported. Missing metadata, open-collector/open-emitter pins, multiple supplies, unconnected supplies, and unrecognized functions are skipped.
A direct SPI signal net between two receivers or two drivers is not reported because electrical direction is ambiguous. Bidirectional pairs are skipped when both orientations are plausible.
Return-like power-input pins are excluded by exact return-like function or net-name context; custom ground aliases may be treated as supplies or make the candidate inapplicable.

The prompt does not model analog or open-drain buses, level translators, power sequencing, loading, timing, transients, off-board devices, PCB copper, or physical continuity. Complete exact LINT-061 mappings carry the sourced compatibility comparison; this rule remains review-only by default.

rules.title: UART-like peers use different voltage-named supply rails
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including complete native pin-type inventories, exact TX/RX-like pin functions, pin/net assignments, and an optional source-hashed digital-peer voltage contract
rules.predicate: For fitted U- or IC-prefixed parts with complete native pin-type inventories and exactly one assigned positive power_in rail per part, report a REVIEW prompt when an exact recognized UART-like TX function joins an output-capable pin to an RX function on an input-capable pin and the two rail labels each contain exactly one explicit positive voltage token with different parsed nominal values. Suppress only exact endpoint/net/symbol/footprint matches with complete authored LINT-061 output and input limits.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Voltage values are parsed from exactly one token in each native net name and are review clues only; they do not establish actual rail voltage, source validity, tolerance, logic thresholds, output guarantees, or incompatibility.

Only U/IC references, the bounded UART/USART TX/RX spelling set, matching native output/input direction, complete pin-type inventories, and one assigned power_in supply net are supported. Missing metadata, open-collector/open-emitter pins, multiple supplies, unconnected supplies, and unrecognized functions are skipped.

The prompt does not model analog or open-drain buses, level translators, power sequencing, loading, timing, transients, off-board devices, PCB copper, or physical continuity. Complete exact LINT-061 mappings carry the sourced compatibility comparison; this rule remains review-only by default.

rules.title: UART-linked peers use different explicit reference nets
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including complete native pin inventories, exact TX/RX-like pin functions or bounded channel labels, native electrical types, and unique net assignments
rules.predicate: For directionally clear native UART TX-to-RX links among fitted U/IC components and bounded or project-reviewed connector candidates, or direct fitted U/IC pairs joined by one uniquely numbered UART/USART TX and RX channel-label pair, require complete component pin/function/type inventories and explicit signal-reference pins of power_in or passive type. Report a REVIEW prompt when each endpoint's signal-reference pins share one unique native net and the two endpoint nets differ. Suppress only a source-current direct serial map that exactly matches both endpoint identities, signal pins/nets, and explicit reference-pin assignments under common_net or separate_nets policy.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The prompt does not decide whether the references should be common, bonded through a component, or intentionally isolated; net names and symbol pin functions provide review clues only.

The native-function path accepts supported UART/USART TX/RX pin-function spellings. The label path accepts only numbered UART/USART TX/RX labels where each net joins exactly one pin from the same two fitted U/IC components. It does not treat connector endpoints or multi-hop translated paths as direct peers. Each endpoint must have a complete native pin inventory plus uniquely assigned GND/AGND/DGND/PGND/VSS/0V/RTN/RETURN/GROUND pins of passive or power_in type. Functions marked SHIELD, CHASSIS, FRAME, or PE are excluded; incomplete, DNP, mixed-reference-domain, third-party, or ambiguous endpoints are skipped.

An exact authored direct serial map records reviewed schematic intent but cannot prove a fitted net tie, PCB copper continuity, an external bond, connector wiring, or electrical suitability. Other maps and stale or partial assignments do not suppress the prompt.

rules.title: USB peers use different explicit reference nets
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist, including complete native pin inventories, supported USB 2.0 D+/D− or bounded USB SuperSpeed pin functions, exact native net membership for direct SuperSpeed pairs, direct or one-fitted-Device:R-per-line USB 2.0 paths, exact map-backed inline-component paths, explicit passive or power-input reference pins, and unique net assignments
rules.predicate: For a fitted numeric or reviewed connector candidate and a fitted U/IC PHY, recognize supported USB 2.0 D+ and D− paths plus bounded direct USB SuperSpeed complementary pairs. USB 2.0 paths retain the existing direct, one-fitted-resistor, exact-mapped-inline, and exact-mapped-protection-shunt rules. For SuperSpeed, require complete native pin inventories and function/type metadata, exactly one positive and one negative pin per endpoint family, connector TX to PHY RX or connector RX to PHY TX, matching positive and negative nets, and exactly the two endpoint pins on each net. Both endpoint reference pins must have explicit passive/power_in functions assigned to one unique net per endpoint. Emit a default REVIEW prompt when those reference nets differ; common reference is quiet. USB 2.0 maps suppress only when their exact data topology and reference policy match. A superspeed_interfaces map suppresses only when one exact direct SuperSpeed path, both endpoint identities, all mapped data/reference pins and nets, and the reviewed reference policy match. A stale map is reported by bus.usb_data_path_mismatch.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Separate reference nets can be intentional, joined elsewhere, or linked by a designed bond; the finding asks for review and does not declare that they must be common.

USB 2.0 coverage includes direct paths, paths through exactly one complete fitted two-pin Device:R per line, paths through one complete inline component with a current exact project map, or direct paths with exact project-mapped multi-pin protection shunts. USB SuperSpeed coverage is limited to one distinct P/N pair family per endpoint, a direct unbranched connector-TX-to-PHY-RX or connector-RX-to-PHY-TX path, and exact two-pin membership on each data net. A matching superspeed_interfaces entry can record an exact common_net, separate_nets, or bonded reference decision; it does not prove bond conduction or PCB copper continuity. A stale or absent map leaves the separate-reference path as REVIEW. Lane-indexed USB-C pairs, muxes, retimers, other multi-lane or multi-hop paths, series components, shunts, arbitrary signal-net peers, incomplete or ambiguous metadata, mixed reference domains, and DNP endpoints are skipped.

Reference pins use bounded return-like function tokens such as GND, AGND, DGND, PGND, VSS, 0V, RTN, RETURN, or GROUND, including numeric suffixes and GND_A/GND_D/GND_P or VSSA/VSSD/VSSP forms; they must be passive or power_in type. Shield, chassis, frame, and protective-earth functions are excluded.

An exact USB data map records source-reviewed schematic intent and compares the named reference pins and nets, but does not prove a fitted bond, PCB copper continuity, external grounding, connector wiring, or electrical suitability.

A bonded USB map is checked separately by bus.usb_data_path_mismatch against exact native component and pin-to-net assignments; the peer-reference review itself does not establish bond conduction or PCB copper continuity.

rules.title: Mapped crystal load network differs from the authored requirement
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored oscillator, resonator, pin, capacitor-value, target-load, and stray-capacitance map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native XML netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For an explicitly mapped two-capacitor Pierce network, report mismatched oscillator or resonator value, symbol, or footprint, mapped-pin assignment, DNP state, unsupported capacitance value, nominal capacitor value outside its authored bounds, a potential unlisted two-pin capacitor directly across an oscillator node and the reference net, or calculated nominal effective load outside the authored target. The estimate is C1*C2/(C1+C2) plus the authored stray-capacitance range.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The check does not infer a crystal from reference prefixes, part values, or symbol descriptions; only project-mapped networks are in scope.
Only explicit pF, nF, uF, and KiCad p/n/u value suffixes are parsed. Unsupported spellings remain incomplete review evidence.

The calculation uses nominal capacitor values and the project-authored stray-capacitance range; it does not model capacitor tolerances or prove startup, frequency accuracy, drive level, ESR margin, parasitics, layout quality, or environmental performance.

rules.title: Mapped regulator feedback divider differs from the authored output requirement
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored regulator and divider map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native XML netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For an explicitly mapped conventional adjustable regulator, report a changed regulator or resistor identity, missing or not-fitted mapped component, wrong output/reference pin net, split or shorted feedback node, unsupported or out-of-range nominal resistance, an additional recognized fitted direct resistor touching the feedback node, or a calculated nominal output interval outside the authored target. The estimate is Vref*(1+Rupper/Rlower) using source-bound nominal resistor values and authored feedback-reference bounds.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule only checks explicitly mapped conventional non-inverting two-resistor feedback dividers; it does not infer adjustable or fixed regulators from reference prefixes, symbol descriptions, values, or part names.

Only supported conventional resistor values and recognized fitted direct resistor references are included; resistor arrays, alternate feedback topologies, or unrecognized branches remain outside coverage.

The calculation uses nominal schematic resistor values and authored reference-voltage bounds; it does not model resistor tolerance, feedback bias current, stability, compensation, startup, load response, device ratings, or PCB feedback routing.

rules.title: Mapped first-order RC filter differs from the authored requirement
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored resistor, capacitor, and pin map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native XML netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For an explicitly mapped series-resistor/shunt-capacitor low-pass, report changed identity, symbol, footprint, pin inventory, assignment, or DNP state; unsupported or out-of-range nominal values; an additional recognized fitted direct passive across mapped nodes; or a calculated nominal 1/(2*pi*R*C) corner outside the authored target.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule checks only project-mapped first-order series-R/shunt-C networks. It does not infer filters from references, values, or signal names, and does not model active, higher-order, or alternate topologies.

Only recognized two-pin resistor and capacitor references with supported nominal value spellings can be included in the extra-component scan; arrays, hidden paths, and unrecognized branches can evade it.
The nominal estimate does not model source/load impedance, component tolerance, transient behavior, anti-alias performance, PCB copper, or analog-front-end safety.

rules.title: Mapped interface exceeds its signal-to-return contact ratio
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored connector interface pin-role catalog and return-distribution threshold compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native XML netlist evidence
rules.predicate: For each explicitly mapped connector whose interface is configured with a minimum signal-contact scope and maximum signal-to-return contact ratio, count pins explicitly classified as signal or return and report an undefined or greater-than-allowed ratio. Require explicit roles for every mapped interface pin; exclude supply, shield, and other roles from the ratio.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The rule runs only for project-configured interfaces and uses explicit interface-catalog pin roles; it does not infer connector roles from symbol functions, pin names, net names, or connector type.
The ratio is an authored review threshold, not a universal electrical standard. It does not require return contacts to share a net or establish a common, bonded, or isolated ground domain.
Contact counts do not prove return-current capacity, PCB copper continuity, shield termination, chassis bonding, isolation, off-board wiring, or physical connector assembly.

rules.title: Mapped external protection entry path needs review
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored exact connector and protection PCB pad map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native connectivity snapshot schema 10
rules.predicate: For each configured channel, compare connector and protection signal/reference pad identities, footprints, fitted state, expected nets, and native copper connectivity. Apply only the authored connector-to-protector pad-center distance and reference-pad connected-via count/radius limits.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 native pcbnew API; each configured project's exact version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: The project owns the exact PCB pad mapping, expected nets, and any thresholds; the rule does not infer ESD devices, ground nets, required connection, or universal spacing/via-count targets.

Straight-line pad-center distance does not measure routed copper length, route order, current density, parasitic inductance, or transient response. Connected-via counts describe only the native copper component at the mapped reference pad.
A passing map does not establish device suitability, clamp performance, full transient interception, electrical approval, or manufacturing readiness.

rules.title: Mapped decoupling capacitor placement needs review
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored IC and capacitor pad mapping compared with source-bound KiCad 10 pcbnew geometry/connectivity snapshot schema 10
rules.predicate: For each explicitly mapped IC supply/return pin pair, compare fitted exact-footprint capacitor pin pairs on the declared supply and return nets, verify native copper connectivity to the IC pins, and measure Euclidean center-to-center distance from IC supply pad to capacitor supply pad. When configured, also measure from the capacitor return-pad center to the nearest via listed in that pad's native copper-connectivity component. Apply only authored maximum distances and the any/all candidate policy.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 native pcbnew API; each configured project's exact version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: Only exact project-mapped IC and capacitor pins are checked. The rule does not infer decoupling components or power-pin roles from values, references, net names, or footprints.

The Euclidean supply-pad and optional return-via center distances do not model the complete supply/return loop, plane reference, trace inductance, capacitor value or bias derating, resonance, or transient performance.
A passing configured threshold is only a project-selected placement screen. It is not a universal limit and does not prove electrical adequacy or manufacturing quality.

rules.title: Mapped PCB net contains a track below its authored width screen
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored net-width map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 pcbnew track inventory in connectivity snapshot schema 6
rules.predicate: For each explicitly mapped net, compare every native KiCad track item's integer-nanometer width with that net's project-authored minimum micrometer screen; report exact track UUID, layer, width, and endpoint coordinates, or incomplete coverage when no native track item is assigned to the net.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 native pcbnew API; each configured project's exact version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: Only project-mapped net names and native track-item widths are checked; the rule does not infer rails or intended current from net names or topology.
The screen does not calculate ampacity, temperature rise, pulse-current limits, plane spreading, via bottlenecks, or electrical performance.
A net with no track items may use zones or have no routed copper; report incomplete coverage rather than treating either case as a width pass or defect.

rules.title: Mapped PCB signal track has limited adjacent reference-copper coverage
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored signal/reference net and layer map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 pcbnew track and filled-zone contours in current connectivity snapshot schema 10
rules.predicate: For each mapped straight track meeting the authored minimum length, measure the exact centerline fraction inside the union of same-net filled-zone polygons on each immediately adjacent copper layer. A track is below threshold only when every adjacent layer misses the authored fraction. Tracks below the minimum are always identified; when review_excluded_short_tracks is true, any such exclusion leaves the configured coverage incomplete.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 native pcbnew API; each configured project's exact version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: Only exact project-mapped signal nets and route layers are checked; the rule does not infer signal roles, expected reference nets, or thresholds from names.

The metric follows track centerlines, not trace-width overlap or return-current fields. Pad and via clearances count as uncovered; arcs and routes with no supported measured segments remain incomplete.

Segments shorter than the project-authored minimum are excluded from the fraction. Their exact track IDs remain in coverage evidence; projects can opt to turn any exclusion into a REVIEW coverage gap with review_excluded_short_tracks.

A mapped endpoint via whose center falls inside a mapped reference-zone hole is reported as possible antipad context, but the hole may contain clearance from other geometry; the interval remains uncovered and can still create a review false positive.

Filled copper along a segment does not prove plane continuity to endpoint pads, connectivity between plane islands or layers, return-current adequacy, emissions, or electrical performance. Thresholds are project-authored review screens, not universal limits.

rules.title: Mapped switching-current loop and return plane need review
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored exact pad order and return-plane layer compared with source-bound KiCad 10 pcbnew snapshot schema 10, including native track endpoint contacts and canonical filled-zone island contours
rules.predicate: For each explicit switching-loop pad order, verify exact footprint, net, fitted state, and unique native pad center; compute the integer shoelace area of the authored pad-center polygon, compare it with an optional project limit, verify that mapped return pads share one filled island, and optionally resolve project-mapped trace edges into unique native track chains with ordered vertices and lengths.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 native pcbnew API; each configured project's exact version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: The loop-area metric is only a polygon through project-authored pad centers. Explicit trace edges report per-edge centerlines and lengths, and plane edges report one exact shared filled-island contour area; the analyzer does not calculate a full routed-loop area or connect trace geometry through component internals.

Trace edges require an exact project-mapped net and copper-layer scope and exactly one native path. Missing contacts, branch ambiguity, multiple paths, unsupported arcs, out-of-scope vias, or stale pad mapping remain incomplete.

The return-plane result requires all mapped pads to touch one same-net filled zone island on one declared copper layer. Routes formed from multiple zones/tracks can remain incomplete even when the overall net is connected.

The check does not establish parasitics, switching behavior, emissions, stability, thermal performance, manufacturing quality, or electrical suitability of the project-selected threshold. Hardware or simulation validation remains separate.

rules.title: Authored differential-pair constraints lack exact active native DRC coverage
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored differential-pair rule map compared with source-bound KiCad 10 .kicad_dru rules, .kicad_pro severity settings, native DRC report, and native validation summary
rules.predicate: For every explicitly mapped positive/negative net pair and required track-width, pair-gap, skew, or uncoupled-length bound, require exactly one native rule with condition A.inDiffPair('<pair selector>') and exact integer-nanometer bounds; report missing, mismatched, duplicate, ignored, unsupported, or unrecognized pair-name coverage.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export

The v1 rule parser supports exact A.inDiffPair('<selector>') conditions, mm or mil lengths that convert to integer nanometers, and pair suffixes _P/_N or +/-; other condition expressions or naming schemes remain uncovered.

A matching rule does not prove the project-authored limit is appropriate for the interface, stack-up, impedance, or signal-integrity target. Additional unconfigured rules are not independently evaluated by this audit.

rules.title: Mapped PCB signal paths lack exact native DRC length or skew coverage
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored exact PCB pad paths and bundles compared with source-bound KiCad 10 DRC rules, DRC receipt, native PCB connectivity snapshot, and schematic netlist
rules.predicate: For each mapped exact pad-to-pad path, require matching source-netlist and PCB pad assignments, non-DNP endpoints in one native copper component, and exactly one active A.fromTo rule with the authored length bounds; for each bundle, require the native wildcard endpoint set to equal the mapped endpoint set and exactly one active A.fromTo skew rule with the authored maximum.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: This audits project-authored rule coverage and native endpoint connectivity only. KiCad native DRC remains responsible for measuring actual route length and skew.
A matching rule does not prove the authored endpoints, length limit, or skew limit are appropriate for the interface, timing budget, impedance, stack-up, or electrical safety target.

Bundle pad selectors must resolve exactly to the mapped fitted board endpoints. Other condition syntax, incomplete netlists, non-mapped paths, off-board wiring, and physical continuity remain outside this audit.

rules.title: Named PCB keepout areas differ from reviewed geometry intent
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored named keepout signature compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native PCB rule-area geometry, copper layers, and restriction flags
rules.predicate: For each mapped named copper keepout, require exactly one native rule area with the reviewed canonical outline-and-hole digest, exact copper-layer set, and exact track/via/pad/zone-fill/footprint restriction flags; missing, duplicate, renamed, reshaped, layer-changed, or restriction-changed areas remain incomplete.

A project owner must author the mapped area name, signature, copper layers, restriction flags, and basis from an independent approved source. A stale or inaccurate contract can preserve the wrong geometry.

This compares authored KiCad rule-area definitions only. It does not prove that the rule area covers an external datasheet region, that all relevant copper layers are enabled or included, or that fabricated copper and assembly match the source.

rules.title: RF module identity, feed, and placement-relative antenna keepout differ from the project requirement
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored exact module identity, RF feed, antenna disposition, and footprint-local keepout compared with native schematic netlist and KiCad 10 PCB snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
rules.predicate: For each explicitly mapped RF module, compare symbol, footprint, optional PART_ID, fitted/DNP state, and RF feed pin/net with the native schematic and board. For onboard antennas, transform the independently authored module-local polygons through the exact native footprint position, orientation, and front/back side, then require exactly one named native rule area with matching geometry, copper layers, and restrictions.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; placement-relative evidence requires native PCB snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
limitations: The project owner must explicitly identify each RF module, exact symbol and footprint, fitted disposition, feed pin/net, and local keepout from an approved independent requirement. The check does not infer RF modules from names or decide which grounds, antenna regions, or RF paths should be common.

The geometry comparison verifies authored rule-area definitions after applying KiCad's observed footprint transform. It does not validate antenna performance, impedance, radiation pattern, data-sheet interpretation, copper not represented by the rule area, or fabricated hardware.
Only explicit onboard-antenna, external-antenna, and DNP dispositions are supported. Unsupported board snapshot versions and missing source evidence remain incomplete or blocked.

rules.title: Configured pad-to-reference-copper clearance is below its project minimum
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored exact pad, schematic net, reference copper net, copper layer, and minimum gap compared with source-bound KiCad 10 native PCB snapshot schema 14
rules.predicate: For each explicitly mapped pad, require the exact schematic pin assignment and native PCB pad net to match the authored signal net. Measure the effective native pad shape to filled zone copper on the authored reference net and copper layer after KiCad zone refill. Emit a review candidate when that evidence is incomplete or when the measured minimum distance is below the project-authored positive threshold.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 digest-pinned pcbnew profiles; exact project version and image are checked
limitations: The project owner must identify each exact pad, expected schematic net, reference copper net, layer, and approved minimum from an independent requirement. The heuristic cannot infer which connector pads should share a ground domain or decide that similarly named nets must be connected.

The probe measures the nearest matching filled zone on the selected layer. It does not establish that the zone is bonded to a connector return, validate electrical performance or touch sensing, or prove fabricated copper geometry.

Missing pads, unsupported layers, absent reference zones, empty fills, source-net disagreement, and unsupported snapshot evidence remain incomplete or blocked. A completed measurement is review evidence and is not electrical or manufacturing approval.

rules.title: Schematic and native PCB component inventory differ
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound native schematic netlist compared with exact KiCad native PCB footprint snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
rules.predicate: For each schematic component with a nonempty assigned footprint that is not marked DNP, compare its reference case-insensitively with the native PCB footprint inventory. Report a review candidate when the reference is absent or when the exact assigned footprint identity differs from the placed native footprint identity.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: The check does not infer whether a fitted schematic component is intended to be off-board or whether two different footprint identities are geometrically equivalent. Projects can suppress a reviewed exception with the existing exact-fingerprint ignore lifecycle.

Only missing references and exact assigned-footprint identity differences are reported. Board-only mechanical footprints, schematic/PCB value differences, schematic/board DNP disagreements, pad equivalence, and physical assembly state are outside this predicate; value and DNP differences have dedicated rules.
The check requires a source-bound netlist and KiCad PCB footprint inventory snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14. Missing, stale, or unsupported evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: PCB footprint reference has no schematic counterpart
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound native schematic netlist compared with exact KiCad native PCB footprint snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
rules.predicate: For each native PCB footprint with a nonempty reference, compare its reference case-insensitively with all source-bound schematic netlist component references. Report a review candidate when no schematic component has the same reference.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: This is an opt-in review heuristic. It cannot determine whether an unmatched board footprint is an error or an intentional mechanical, fabrication, fiducial, or other board-only item.

The check compares reference identity only. It does not infer electrical role, assembly state, footprint correctness, or manufacturing intent. Project owners can suppress an intentional reference with the existing exact-fingerprint ignore lifecycle.

The check requires a source-bound schematic netlist and native PCB footprint inventory snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14. Missing, stale, or unsupported evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: Project-required PCB component is not fitted as specified
rules.evidence_adapter: Project-authored required-reference map compared with source-bound native schematic netlist and exact KiCad PCB footprint snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
rules.predicate: For each reference in the project-authored required fitted-reference map, require a matching non-DNP schematic component and native PCB footprint with the exact mapped footprint ID. When supplied, also require exact native symbol and PART_ID identity. Report each missing or DNP reference and each identity mismatch; do not infer requirements from similar components.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: The map is an independently authored project requirement for the base assembly. A missing map is not evidence that all project components are required; if the rule is explicitly enabled without a map, coverage blocks.

The check compares exact case-insensitive reference identity and exact footprint, optional symbol, optional PART_ID, and DNP values. It does not infer fitted parts from matching peers, validate the requirement against a BOM or approval record, resolve assembly variants, or prove physical population.

The check requires a source-bound native netlist digest and KiCad PCB footprint snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14. Missing, stale, duplicate, or unsupported evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: Schematic and PCB DNP states differ
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound base schematic netlist and PCB snapshot plus paired exact-version schematic netlist and PCB position exports for each declared named variant
rules.predicate: For each case-insensitive schematic reference with a nonempty assigned footprint and a matching placed PCB footprint, compare base schematic and native PCB DNP flags. For each project-declared named variant present on the native board, export both artifacts using the same exact variant name; compare schematic netlist DNP state with native PCB DNP state inferred from all-position references minus --exclude-dnp references. Report only mismatches.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: This compares CAD DNP flags only; it does not establish the physical assembly population or whether a board placement should exist.

Named-variant checks run only for names declared in schematic.variants and independently confirmed present on the native PCB. If a declared name is absent from the board, coverage is BLOCKED and no default-variant fallback is compared.

Variant board population is inferred from the same-name KiCad position exports: all listed references minus references exported with --exclude-dnp. References absent from either compared artifact and schematic symbols without an assigned footprint are outside the comparison.
Missing placements remain with pcb.schematic_component_inventory.
The check requires a source-bound netlist and KiCad PCB footprint inventory snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14. Missing, stale, or unsupported evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: Schematic and PCB component value fields differ
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound schematic netlist value fields compared with KiCad native PCB footprint value fields in snapshot schema 13 or later
rules.predicate: For each case-insensitive reference with a nonempty schematic footprint assignment that is fitted in both sources, compare the schematic component value with the placed native PCB footprint value after trimming surrounding whitespace. Report only exact text differences.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: This compares two CAD text fields. It does not establish electrical equivalence, component identity, assembly intent, physical population, or whether a displayed value is required on the board.

The check is case-sensitive and reports formatting differences after trimming surrounding whitespace. Approved board-specific labels and intentional alternate text may be ignored by exact fingerprint or disabled through the project rule mode.

Only references present and footprint-assigned in the schematic and placed in the PCB are compared. DNP components, mismatched population states, off-board components, board-only footprints, and named design-variant values are outside this comparison.
The check requires a source-bound schematic netlist and native PCB footprint value snapshot schema 13 or later. Missing, stale, or older snapshot evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: Schematic pin and PCB pad net assignments differ
rules.evidence_adapter: Source-bound native schematic netlist pin assignments compared with native PCB pad assignments in snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14
rules.predicate: For each pin with an assigned schematic net or an explicit native unconnected-net assignment, compare the case-insensitive reference and exact pin number with the same-numbered native PCB pad when the schematic footprint assignment is nonempty, the PCB reference is placed, and both footprint IDs match after trimming. Report a missing board pad, an unassigned board pad, a different exact net name, or a PCB net assigned to a schematic-unconnected pin.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10.0.0 and 10.0.5 native pcbnew API; exact project version and digest-pinned image are checked
limitations: This compares CAD net assignments by reference and pad number. It does not infer that repeated connector pins, USB/serial returns, or similarly named nets must be bonded, and it does not establish routed copper continuity or physical conduction.

A schematic pin number may not map one-to-one to a physical pad in a custom symbol or footprint. Alternate pin-to-pad mappings, schematic-only symbols, board-only pads, and mismatched footprint identities are outside this comparison; confirm prompts against the part's approved mapping.
DNP placements are compared when present in both sources because this is a CAD assignment check; the result does not establish physical population or a named variant's effective pin assignment.
Exact net names are compared after native netlist normalization. Intentional aliases or board-side net naming differences may need project review, an exact finding ignore, or rule mode override.
The check requires source-bound schematic assignments and native PCB footprint/pad snapshot schema 12, 13, or 14. Missing, stale, or unsupported evidence is a coverage gap and never a clean result.

rules.title: Supported two-pin LED directly spans a positive rail and return
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For a fitted exact Device:LED symbol with exactly two inventoried pins, report when both pins have unique, distinct native net assignments and one net has an exclusive recognized positive-rail role while the other has an exclusive recognized return role.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Only the exact Device:LED symbol identity is recognized. Custom LED symbols, addressable LEDs, multi-die symbols, and unsupported or incomplete pin inventories are outside the predicate.

A direct schematic rail-to-return assignment prompts review; it does not establish forward polarity, source voltage/current, integrated or off-board current limiting, a required resistor value, operating safety, or PCB copper connectivity.

Only the existing power_function_key and return-like net/function recognizers classify the two endpoints. Custom names without recognized native symbol pin functions can evade the candidate; ambiguous nets with both roles are excluded.

rules.title: Output-capable pin directly drives a two-pin LED to a rail
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For a fitted exact Device:LED, or a custom identity whose exact PART_ID, native symbol, footprint, and complete two-pin number/function/electrical-type inventory match a project-authored led role binding, report when the two distinct LED terminal nets include a fitted native output, bidirectional, tri_state, open_collector, or open_emitter pin on one side and an exclusive recognized positive-rail or return role on the other. An exact project-authored power path ending at a current_controlled_sink may suppress only the matching standard LED A-to-K path when the source-bound endpoint identity and pin signature match.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Custom symbols participate only through an opt-in project role map bound to exact PART_ID, native symbol, footprint, and the complete two-pin number/function/electrical-type inventory. Missing or stale identities block lint and do not receive the role. Unmapped symbols, missing pin-type metadata, DNP parts, ambiguous rails, and other resistor-separated rail paths are outside the predicate. A visible fitted positive-value resistor from an intermediate return-like LED net to a distinct recognized return suppresses this direct-path prompt.

A finding is a review prompt, not proof that current limiting is absent or required. An output may be internally current-limited, an LED may have other assembly-level protection, and off-board paths are not modeled.

Current-controlled-sink suppression is explicit project metadata, not an inference. The mapped path must match the native PART_ID, output pin function and electrical type, exact LED reference, A/K pin polarity, and source/net topology. This match does not establish current regulation, current limits, brightness, or electrical adequacy.

The rule does not infer LED polarity, output voltage/current limits, resistor value or adequacy, PCB copper connectivity, physical population, or runtime behavior. A parallel resistor across the LED and rail does not count as a series element and does not suppress the candidate.

rules.title: Named power pin conflicts with a recognized net role
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each fitted pin with exactly one exported net and a native function recognized by power_function_key or is_return_function, emit a review candidate when a recognized positive-supply function is assigned to a return-like net, or when a recognized return function is assigned to a positive-supply net. Net labels recognized as one role take precedence over attached pin functions; peer-pin evidence is used only when the net name is unrecognized, and the candidate pin never classifies its own net. Connector return pins remain with the connector-specific rule.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: Supply functions are limited to the exact aliases recognized by power_function_key; return functions and net labels use the bounded connector_identity and return_nets recognizers. Unrecognized custom functions or labels can evade the candidate.

Connector return pins are excluded because connector.return_pin_on_positive_rail handles native and source-matched return roles; recognized positive-supply connector pins remain in scope. DNP components and pins with zero or multiple exported net assignments are excluded.

Pin function and net-name evidence do not prove electrical potential, project intent, a required connection, physical population, or PCB copper continuity. This rule is REVIEW by default; a project may apply its normal rule override or exact-fingerprint ignore lifecycle.

rules.title: Named supply pin is assigned to a negative rail label
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each fitted pin with exactly one exported net, report a review candidate when the native pin function is recognized by power_function_key and the assigned net has an explicitly leading minus sign followed by one of the supported numeric voltage rail names. The negative rail recognizer uses only numeric aliases already present in the positive rail catalog; it does not infer polarity from VEE, VSS, NEG labels, or arbitrary text.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The recognized negative labels are limited to -1V8/-1.8V, -2V5/-2.5V, -3V3/-3.3V, -5V/-5.0V, -9V, -12V, -24V, and -48V, including spaces that do not change the token. Custom negative-rail names and negative aliases such as VEE are outside the predicate.

A named function and signed net label are review clues, not proof of potential, symbol correctness, an electrical defect, or project intent. A valid isolated or re-referenced domain may use these names intentionally. The rule does not check rail magnitude, absolute maximum ratings, PCB copper, physical population, or conduction.

rules.title: Recognized IC supply rail has no fitted capacitor to return
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each unique assigned net recognized as a positive supply by power_function_key or an attached native power_in pin function, report fitted non-connector power_in pins when no fitted recognized capacitor-symbol component connects this net to a distinct net with a recognized return-like name or attached pin function. A project may classify an exact custom capacitor for this rule only through component_role_map entries that match PART_ID, native symbol, footprint, and complete two-pin passive inventory.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The review prompt covers native power_in pins on non-connector references and recognizes positive rails via power_function_key plus return-like names or pin functions via is_return_like_net_name. Connector classification is limited to numeric J/P/X/CN references, standard Connector libraries, and exact project-reviewed interface references. Capacitor recognition is limited to common library IDs whose final symbol name is C, begins C_ or CP_, is exactly CP, or contains capacitor.

A capacitor connected between the IC rail and a recognized return-like net does not prove that the device datasheet requires it, that its value is suitable, that it is placed locally on the PCB, or that its physical return path is adequate.

Unrecognized capacitor symbol IDs and custom return labels without a recognized return pin function may create extra review prompts; off-board or internal decoupling may do the same. A custom capacitor counts only when the project's exact role map matches its PART_ID, symbol, footprint, and complete two-pin passive inventory; stale entries block lint, and the role is used only by this decoupling-presence hint. Custom/unrecognized rail names without a recognized power_in function can evade the rule. Explicitly DNP ICs are excluded, and DNP capacitors do not satisfy the presence check. Numeric J/P/X/CN references, standard Connector libraries, and exact project-reviewed connector references are excluded; other unreviewed component identities may be treated as IC candidates.

rules.title: Mapped IC decoupling capacitance is below the project minimum
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each project-authored IC power-pin requirement, verify the exact fitted IC identity, mapped power-pin type and net, and every fitted two-pin capacitor identity, passive pin inventory, pin type, and power/return net assignment. Parse the mapped capacitors' nominal values with the bounded capacitance parser, sum them in pF, and report when the sum is below the independently authored inclusive minimum.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The project must explicitly map the IC identity, one power pin and net, one return net, every capacitor counted toward the requirement, a positive minimum, and the source basis. No IC, rail, capacitor, or threshold is inferred.
A mapped IC marked DNP is a stale requirement and produces a REVIEW mapping finding; its capacitor total is not evaluated.

Only fitted, exact two-pin capacitors with explicitly supported nominal value spellings count. The result does not apply tolerance, DC-bias derating, voltage rating, temperature behavior, placement, current demand, transient response, or PCB return-path evidence.

A passing result establishes only the authored nominal schematic comparison. It does not establish that the source basis is correct, that the map covers every relevant IC pin, or that the physical design meets an electrical requirement.

rules.title: Mapped series power path differs from the schematic
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each project-authored path with exact endpoint and two-terminal component identities, report when an endpoint or required element is absent or ambiguous, marked DNP, has a different symbol or footprint, lacks its mapped pin in the native inventory, or assigns a mapped pin to a different net. Optional endpoint PART_ID, native pin function, and electrical type constraints are checked when supplied; a current_controlled_sink endpoint requires all three.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: The map covers only its explicitly listed endpoints, two-terminal elements, and ordered net chain; it does not discover expected paths or detect unlisted parallel paths.

A current_controlled_sink endpoint is an owner-authored role label. Its exact PART_ID and native pin signature validate identity and connectivity only; they do not prove that the component regulates current or is suitable for an LED load.
A passing schematic comparison does not establish component conduction or suitability, datasheet pinout truth, PCB copper continuity, external wiring, current capacity, or physical population.

The map is not a current-direction or power-source inference. Switching devices, multi-pin protection networks, alternate assembly states, and direct same-net paths need separate explicit requirements.

rules.title: Mapped power-sequence dependency differs from the schematic
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each project-authored stage and power-good-to-enable dependency, report a missing or ambiguous component, mismatched symbol, footprint or optional PART_ID, DNP stage, missing mapped native pin, or changed output/control pin net. Report cycles in the explicitly authored dependency graph and cycles in output-to-enable net assignments only when every participating exact mapped stage matches the native netlist.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: This opt-in map checks only listed stage output, power-good, and enable endpoints and listed dependency edges. The output-to-enable cycle prompt needs exact matching maps for participating stages; an absent map or omitted stage is not inferred from EN/PG names or device families.

A matching netlist proves only the listed schematic pin/net assignments. It does not verify the requirement source, silicon behavior, rail ramp or startup timing, thresholds, firmware state transitions, brownout behavior, electrical suitability, external control, or PCB copper continuity.

Firmware, external, always-on, or unmodeled enable control is owner-declared context and is not behaviorally checked. Numeric timing bounds and source-backed calculations are outside this first version.

rules.title: Decoupled power input has no recognized source anchor or path
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each fitted internal native power_in pin on a net with a fitted, exactly inventoried two-terminal capacitor to a recognized return, emit a review candidate when no recognized positive-rail net or fitted power_out pin provides a source anchor, or when a source anchor exists but no supported passive path reaches one. Supported paths use fitted, exactly inventoried two-pin Device:R variants parsed at <= 1 ohm, Device:L variants, Device:FerriteBead, Device:Fuse, Device:Polyfuse, the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_2_Bridged symbol with native pins 1/2 mapped to A/B, the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged12 symbol with complete pins 1/2/3 mapped to A/C/B and only pins 1/2 bridged, the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged123 symbol with the same complete mapping and all three pins bridged, and exact Device:D or Device:D_Schottky symbols whose native pin functions uniquely identify A and K. Recognized jumper pins each require one assigned net. Bridged solder jumpers are bidirectional; diodes are traversed in their source-to-load conducting direction. A project-authored power-path map suppresses this candidate for its explicitly mapped load endpoints so the precise mismatch report is not duplicated.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: A recognized positive net name is treated as a source anchor even when its physical source is external or absent. A custom-named external source without an attached fitted power_out pin now produces a source-anchor coverage REVIEW; the prompt does not prove the source or rail is missing.

The predicate runs only for internal power_in pins with a fitted capacitor to a recognized return. Capacitor symbols are limited to common C, CP, and capacitor-named library symbols. Connector exclusions use numeric J/P/X/CN references, standard Connector libraries, and exact project-reviewed interface references; custom unreviewed symbols can still be treated as internal loads.

An opaque custom capacitor symbol name is not counted as capacitor evidence. When the supply net is otherwise recognized by the existing IC decoupling rule, that separate rule may independently report missing recognizable capacitor evidence.

Only fitted, exactly inventoried two-terminal low-resistance resistors, inductors, ferrite beads, fuses, polyfuses, the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_2_Bridged identity with native pins 1/2 mapped to A/B, and the exact Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged12 or Jumper:SolderJumper_3_Bridged123 identities with complete native pins 1/2/3 mapped to A/C/B count as bidirectional paths. Bridged12 joins only pins 1 and 2; Bridged123 joins all three. Open, DNP, other, or ambiguously mapped solder jumpers remain unsupported and may produce extra review prompts. Exact Device:D and Device:D_Schottky identities count only with one native A pin and one native K pin on distinct nets, and only in the source-to-load direction. Zener, TVS, custom diode, switch, regulator, semiconductor, and ambiguous-pin paths remain unsupported and may produce extra review prompts.

A fitted power_out pin counts as a source anchor even when a regulator, switch, or other device is not operational. The finding does not prove that a connection is required, that a component conducts, or that current direction, electrical ratings, PCB copper, off-board wiring, assembly state, or manufacturing are valid.

rules.title: Connector/capacitor-only net has no visible local DC anchor
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist
rules.predicate: For each non-return net, emit a review candidate when every fitted assigned pin belongs to a recognized connector or supported capacitor symbol and the net contains at least one pin of each; DNP references are excluded, and any unknown or other fitted component pin suppresses the candidate.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; the selected project's exact catalogued version is checked before export
limitations: A connector can receive its DC level from an off-board host, and an IC can have internal bias; the candidate does not establish that a local bias is required or missing.

The rule checks only the native pins assigned to one schematic net. It does not trace a complete DC path, evaluate component states or values, identify an analog function, or prove PCB and off-board connectivity.
Capacitor recognition is limited to Device:C, Device:CP, and library symbol IDs containing Capacitor. Unknown capacitor aliases and symbol metadata are skipped or suppress a candidate.

Any additional fitted non-connector, non-capacitor pin suppresses the candidate, even when that component does not provide a DC reference; DNP pins are excluded. Connector identity uses the bounded automatic candidate set and exact project-reviewed interface references.
Return-like nets and pins with return-like function names are excluded. Custom return names, external circuitry, internal pulls, resistor arrays, and component-internal paths are not modeled.

rules.title: STM32 CubeMX pin map differs from the KiCad schematic
rules.evidence_adapter: KiCad 10 native XML netlist normalized by kicad_tooling.validate.read_netlist plus a project-local, SHA-256-bound STM32CubeMX IOC file
rules.predicate: A project-mapped package port pin is absent, has a different CubeMX Signal or checked GPIO_Label, maps to the wrong KiCad symbol pin, has a different schematic net, or belongs to a different MCU part/symbol; a bounded STM32 identity hint requests a map when no contract exists.
supported_kicad_versions: KiCad 10 CLI profile; each project native receipt verifies its exact catalogued KiCad version before netlist comparison
limitations: STM32 discovery uses only the literal STM32 token in component value or symbol ID and can miss other MCU families or nonstandard identities.
The project must author a complete package-pin inventory, map each signal pin to a symbol pin, and cite the reviewed pinout basis; the check cannot establish that the authored package map is correct.
The rule compares selected IOC Signal and GPIO_Label values. It does not compile firmware, validate silicon capabilities, prove PCB routing, or establish off-board behavior.

Only the bounded UTF-8 line syntax for CubeMX .Signal and .GPIO_Label assignments is parsed, including physical-pin alternate-function suffixes with hyphens or escaped spaces; duplicate fields, conflicting raw keys that normalize to one physical pin, and unsupported pin keys block comparison instead of being guessed.
